source_contract.second_class_scope_rule: Accepted Chapter 4 propositions are outside subsections explicitly marked [一等].

review_basis: current official MLIT 第5版 source/locators

decisions.rationale: 4.1 supports powered-lift as the combination of vertical takeoff/landing capability and airplane-like forward cruise; no canonical item tests this hybrid-aircraft proposition.
4.1 states fixed-wing aircraft generally have a safe minimum speed below which low-speed flight is not possible; distinct from Q067's excessive-angle-of-attack stall mechanism.
4.1 states that a properly designed fixed-wing aircraft can enter a glide after thrust loss rather than immediately crash; distinct from emergency-site and autorotation questions.
4.3 maps elevator/pitch, aileron/roll, and rudder/yaw; no canonical fixed-wing control-surface mapping item exists.
4.1 explicitly says flight-control surfaces cease to be effective in stall. Q067 tests the cause/effects of excessive angle of attack, not post-stall controllability.

4.1 compares helicopter and multirotor rotor architecture and states the helicopter's larger single rotor can obtain lift more aerodynamically efficiently; distinct from Q060's airplane-versus-rotorcraft mission tradeoff.
4.1 states that with equal motor performance, more multirotor rotors improve failure tolerance and payload; no canonical item tests this system-level consequence.
4.1 explains multirotor yaw through deliberate imbalance of reaction-torque balance; distinct from Q062 lateral tilt and Q068 helicopter tail-rotor control.
4.1 explicitly maps throttle/rudder/aileron/elevator to multirotor movement. Existing items test actuator flow or one lateral movement, not the complete command mapping.
4.2 requires ground lighting so takeoff/landing, emergency sites and route obstacles remain visible at night; distinct from Q063 vision-sensor limitations and B2 night human factors.
4.2 explicitly provides an exception to the aircraft-light requirement when the flight area is sufficiently illuminated; this equipment-rule boundary is not in the canonical bank.
4.2 no-assistant BVLOS requires continuous monitoring of aircraft along the entire route; distinct from existing ownship state/route-deviation monitoring.
4.2 no-assistant BVLOS includes a manufacturer-certified function intended not to harm third parties; distinct from conspicuity and ownship telemetry coverage.
4.3 directly defines pitch, roll and yaw. Existing control/sensor items use these axes but do not test the definitions themselves.

Q070 already tests the IMU as a 3-axis gyro plus acceleration-sensor system that detects angular velocity and acceleration. C015's answer-defining proposition repeats the acceleration-sensor detection role with only a narrower component framing, so the new reasoning target is insufficiently distinct.

Q043's correct proposition already requires detecting local geomagnetism to obtain heading before magnetic calibration. C016 isolates the same geomagnetic-heading proposition and does not add a sufficiently distinct decision boundary.
4.4 directly distinguishes barometric, ultrasonic and LiDAR altitude-measurement principles; no canonical item tests the sensor-principle mapping.
4.4 gives total battery voltage as per-cell voltage times cell count; distinct from existing storage, swelling, short-circuit and cold-endurance items.
4.4 states that maintaining constant output while discharge voltage drops requires increased current; no canonical power-voltage-current reasoning item exists.
4.4 states usable battery capacity changes with discharge current and temperature. Q045 tests a specific low-temperature endurance consequence, not this broader capacity dependency.
4.4 defines state of charge as current dischargeable charge relative to full-charge dischargeable capacity; no canonical SOC-definition item exists.
4.4 states brushless motors are easier to maintain, quieter and longer-lived; distinct from Q071 ESC function.
4.4 requires rotor/propeller shape to match CW/CCW motor rotation direction; no canonical installation-direction item exists.
4.4 contrasts electric and engine power sources on vibration/noise versus endurance/range; distinct from Q060 airframe-type efficiency.
4.4 explains the apparent post-climb battery drop as transient voltage sag caused by high current; no canonical load-induced voltage-sag item exists.
4.4 states overcharge/overdischarge accelerates LiPo degradation and shortens life; distinct from Q033 swelling replacement and Q072 short-circuit fire.
4.4 requires balance charging and connection of the balance connector for multi-cell LiPo packs; no canonical cell-balance item exists.
4.4 states strong physical impact can cause LiPo fire. Q072 tests short-circuit fire, so the causal hazard is distinct.
4.4 requires manufacturer-specified fuel and specified mixture ratio for engine aircraft; Q079 tests maintenance-provider selection, not fuel specification.
4.5 defines Fresnel-zone clearance and explains that obstacles can reduce field strength, cause errors and shorten range; distinct from Q074 diffraction and Q075 multipath.
